faq.title: How does Facebook know where I am even when I turn off my phone's GPS location?
faq.description: Meta does not rely solely on satellite GPS. When GPS is disabled, Facebook maps your position using your IP address, nearby Wi-Fi network BSSIDs (hardware MAC addresses of routers in range), and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) retail beacons installed in shopping malls and stores. By matching these signals against Meta's global RF mapping databases, Facebook determines your physical location down to the retail aisle.

faq.title: What is 'Off-Facebook Activity' and how does it harvest my browsing habits?
faq.description: Off-Facebook Activity is data that external businesses, retail stores, and websites share with Meta through the embedded Meta Pixel or Conversions API. When you browse shoes on an e-commerce site, book a doctor's appointment, or purchase flight tickets, those external websites beam your identity, purchase amount, and browsing events directly back to Meta's advertising servers.

faq.title: Will clearing my Facebook Location History and Off-Facebook Activity delete my account or photos?
faq.description: No! Clearing location history and disconnecting Off-Facebook Activity purely purges the commercial tracking dossiers Meta built about your external movements and shopping behaviors. Your personal profile, uploaded photo albums, friends list, and messages remain 100% intact, while advertising algorithms are stripped of your behavioral history.

html:
The Omnipresent Surveillance Architecture of Meta

Have you ever experienced an uncanny digital coincidence: you walk into an obscure local coffee shop, browse a pair of boots in a physical downtown retail boutique, or discuss an upcoming vacation with a friend over lunch. Later that evening, you open Facebook or Instagram, and the very first sponsored advertisement is for that exact local coffee shop or that exact brand of footwear.

Many consumers jump to a sensationalized conclusion: "Facebook must be secretly listening through my phone's microphone!" While that myth is widespread, the reality is far more sophisticated, pervasive, and systemic. Meta does not need to waste battery power analyzing noisy audio recordings; it operates the world's most intricate, multi-vector physical and digital surveillance grid.

Through background location geofencing, Wi-Fi router BSSID triangulation, Bluetooth retail beacons, and Off-Facebook Activity tracking pixels embedded across millions of third-party websites, Meta tracks where you sleep, where you work, where you shop, and what medical conditions you research. In this technical guide, we deconstruct Meta's surveillance mechanics and provide a complete, step-by-step blueprint to purge your history and lock down your privacy.

Beyond Satellite GPS: How Meta Tracks Your Physical Movements

A common misconception is that revoking the basic "Location" permission in Android stops Facebook from knowing where you are. In reality, Meta utilizes multiple independent tracking vectors:

  • Wi-Fi BSSID Triangulation: Even if satellite GPS is turned off, your smartphone's Wi-Fi radio continuously listens to beacon frames broadcast by nearby Wi-Fi routers. Each router broadcasts a unique hardware identifier known as a BSSID (Basic Service Set Identifier / MAC Address). Meta maintains a massive global database correlating millions of BSSIDs with exact physical street addresses. If your phone detects the BSSID of a Starbucks router, Meta knows you are inside that Starbucks down to 3-meter accuracy!
  • Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Retail Beacons: High-end shopping malls, department stores, and airports install battery-powered BLE beacons on walls and ceilings. As you walk past a display, the beacon broadcasts micro-signals that the Facebook app registers in the background, logging which retail aisles you spent time browsing.
  • Cell Tower Triangulation & IP Geolocation: Your mobile cellular IP address reveals your regional neighborhood and municipal sector at all times.
  • EXIF Camera Metadata: Whenever you upload a photo to Facebook, the image file contains embedded EXIF metadata (GPS coordinates, camera model, lens focal length, and exact timestamp). Unless stripped, every uploaded photo broadcasts your precise location history.

Off-Facebook Activity: The Commercial Web Scraper

Even more intrusive than physical location tracking is Off-Facebook Activity. Meta does not merely monitor what you do inside its apps; it tracks your behavior across the broader internet:

  1. Over 30% of the world's top websites have embedded the Meta Pixel (a piece of tracking JavaScript code) or the server-side Conversions API into their checkout and browsing pages.
  2. When you search for cancer symptoms on a health portal, apply for a mortgage on a banking website, or purchase running shoes on an e-commerce store, the website sends an encrypted payload to Meta: 
    Payload: { User_Email_Hash: "...", Action: "Viewed_Product", Item: "Running Shoes", Price: "$120" }
  3. Meta matches the hashed customer data to your Facebook profile. In less than two seconds, your external internet history is linked to your advertising profile, triggering highly targeted commercials across Instagram and Facebook.

Comprehensive Comparison Matrix: Meta Tracking Defense Settings

Surveillance Vector Tracking Mechanism Privacy Exposure Level Recommended Defensive Configuration
Background Geofencing Continuous background GPS pings Extreme (Tracks full daily routine) Set to 'Don't Allow' in Android Settings
Precise Location Centimeter-accurate GPS coordinates High (Identifies exact buildings/rooms) Toggle 'Use precise location' to OFF
Off-Facebook Activity Meta Pixel & third-party website APIs Extreme (Harvests web shopping & health) Clear history & Disconnect Future Activity
Location History Vault Meta cloud archive of past movements High (Historical movement dossier) Delete Location History in Accounts Center

Ultrasound Cross-Device Tracking: The Audio Beacon Reality

While the popular myth claims Facebook's app secretly listens to room conversations to target ads, privacy researchers discovered a far more sophisticated acoustic surveillance vector: Ultrasound Cross-Device Tracking (uXDT):

  • Inaudible Acoustic Frequencies: Commercial television commercials, YouTube advertisements, and in-store retail speakers broadcast high-frequency ultrasound audio pulses (between 18 kHz and 22 kHz). These frequencies are completely inaudible to human ears, but perfectly detectable by standard smartphone microphones!
  • Cross-Device Identity Pairing: When an ad plays on your living room television, the inaudible ultrasound beacon embeds an encrypted device identifier. If an ad-tracking SDK inside an open mobile app hears the pulse, it beams a confirmation timestamp to marketing data brokers. The data broker links your living room smart TV, your laptop, and your personal smartphone into a single unified behavioral profile!
  • The Android Solution: In modern Android 12 through Android 15, the operating system displays a prominent green privacy indicator dot in the top-right corner whenever the microphone is accessed. You can verify that Facebook is not accessing your microphone by inspecting Android's Privacy Dashboard.

Stripping EXIF Geolocation Metadata Before Uploading Photos

Every photo captured by your smartphone camera contains embedded Exchangeable Image File Format (EXIF) metadata: exact decimal latitude and longitude coordinates, altitude, compass orientation, camera sensor serial number, and timestamp down to the second.

  • If you upload a vacation photo directly to Facebook, Meta's image ingestion pipeline reads this EXIF data to log your exact physical location, even if you never tagged a location in the post caption!
  • To protect your privacy, install an open-source EXIF stripper like Scrambled Exif (available on F-Droid), or use Android's native share sheet setting to toggle "Remove location from photos" before sharing images to social networks.

Ad Preferences Lockdown: Purging Custom Audience & Lookalike Data

Meta's advertising engine categorizes users through Custom Audiences and Lookalike Modeling. When you purchase items offline at a physical retail store, merchants upload your phone number and email address to Meta as part of a "Custom Audience" list:

  • Auditing Data Providers: Inside Meta's Accounts Center under Ad Preferences > Advertisers you've seen most recently, you can inspect the exact list of corporations that uploaded your contact info to Meta.
  • Revoking Data Broker Profiles: Tap into each advertiser and select "Hide all ads from this advertiser". Under Ad Topics, choose "See less" across invasive behavioral categories: alcohol, parenting, pets, politics, and social issues.
  • Disabling Lookalike Audience Ingestion: By switching your Ad settings to "Not Allowed" for ads based on partner data, you prevent Meta from analyzing your browsing patterns to target ads at your family members and colleagues who share your home Wi-Fi network!
  • Clear Advertising ID on Android: Complete your mobile defense by opening Android Settings > Security & privacy > Ads. Tap "Delete advertising ID". This strips Android of the permanent alphanumeric advertising tracking token that third-party ad brokers use to correlate your device across different installed apps.

Step-by-Step Blueprint: The Complete Facebook Tracking Purge

To permanently sever Meta's surveillance tentacles and purge your movement archives:

Step 1: Revoke Android Operating System Permissions

  1. Open your Android phone's Settings > Apps > Facebook.
  2. Tap Permissions > Location.
  3. Select "Don't allow" (or at minimum, "Allow only while using the app").
  4. Crucially, toggle "Use precise location" to OFF! This prevents Facebook from reading meter-accurate GPS coordinates, restricting it to broad approximate city-level estimates.
  5. Enable "Pause app activity if unused" so Android automatically strips permissions if you don't open Facebook for a month.

Step 2: Purge and Disconnect Off-Facebook Activity

  1. Open the Facebook app and tap the Menu (three lines).
  2. Tap the gear icon to open Settings & Privacy > Settings.
  3. Tap Accounts Center at the very top.
  4. Under Account settings, tap Your information and permissions.
  5. Tap Your activity off Meta technologies:
    • Tap Clear previous activity. Confirm the prompt to permanently purge the historical tracking database.
    • Tap Manage future activity and select "Disconnect future activity"! This instructs Meta's servers to stop linking external website visits to your account moving forward!

Step 3: Delete Location History Archives

  1. In Accounts Center, navigate to Your information and permissions > Location History (or Location Services).
  2. Tap View Location History (enter your account password if prompted).
  3. Tap the three dots in the upper corner and select "Delete all Location History".
  4. Confirm the deletion. All historical GPS traces stored in Meta's cloud vaults will be permanently expunged.

  • Audit Network Sockets: Cut off Facebook's background network telemetry with the best Android firewall apps to block internet per app.
  • Automate Google History Purges: Clean up your search dossier with our guide on Google My Activity and YouTube auto-delete automation.

The Verdict: Reclaiming Physical Sovereignty

Surveillance advertising relies on user passivity: corporations bank on consumers accepting default settings that harvest physical and behavioral telemetry in the background. By revoking Android background location permissions, disabling precise location coordinates, and permanently disconnecting Off-Facebook Activity, you erect an unyielding privacy barrier. Your physical movements through the real world belong to you—not to an advertising conglomerate's algorithmic balance sheet.
